Hi team —

Handoff summary for Lumina Search (context up front so the kickoff can be focused):
- Account: Lumina Search (support site search + in-product recommendation surfaces).
- Index size: ~12M documents (avg tokenized length ~320 tokens; 20% < 120 tokens).
- Current embeddings: 1536-d, produced by their in-house model; they are open to switching to a 1024-d embed model if it materially reduces cost and complexity.
- Primary asks from Lumina: faster nearest-neighbor results for search (p95 latency target 120ms), measurable rerank improvement for top 10 (they want clear uplift vs their current BM25+legacy-ranker baseline), and minimal data exposure during migration.

Key open decisions we should resolve in kickoff:
1) Vector DB preference: managed (Pinecone) vs self-hosted (Milvus on GKE) vs hybrid (hot index in managed + cold in self-hosted). Pros/cons for them are in attachment "lumina_data_inventory.csv".
2) Backfill strategy: full backfill vs staged waves. We should propose a staggered backfill (per-customer shard) to avoid throughput spikes — target window: 7–14 days.
3) Rerank eval design: sample size, metrics, and annotation plan. They asked for nDCG/MAP, but we should define thresholds for acceptance.
4) Security/PII: retention policy and redaction during transfer; Lumina is sensitive about email addresses inside docs.

Immediate asks (for kickoff agenda):
- Marissa: lead implementation plan + staging/backfill cadence (we'll need an ops playbook).
- Ben: capacity estimates and whether Dedicated pools are needed for the backfill window.
- Lumina (Emma/Guillermo): confirm compliance constraints + provide the sample query set (they mentioned a 5k query extract).

Deliverables I will attach to this thread:
- lumina_data_inventory.csv (schema + gross sizes)
- rerank-eval-sample_prompts.md (proposal for sampling and annotation)
- implementation_mop_v1.pdf (redwood recommended playbook template)

Proposed kickoff slots (all PDT): Tue 2026-05-12 10:00–11:00, Wed 2026-05-13 09:00–10:00. Please reply with availability and any extra attendees (security/compliance?).

Camila
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks Camila — great context. Short technical plan for the kickoff so we can be surgical in the meeting: 

1) Staging & backfill approach (proposal):
   - Phase A (staging): index a 10% shard of documents into a staging vectorstore and run smoke tests (latency/load/quality).
   - Phase B (wave backfill): 6 wave approach, each wave ~1.8–2.0M docs over a 24–48 hour window. Throttle backfill to not exceed 30% of steady-state token throughput during the backfill window.
   - Cold storage: move older docs to cold vectorstore (on-prem Milvus) and keep hot index (managed Pinecone) for active docs. This satisfies Lumina's PII constraint while letting us leverage managed inference routing.

2) Vector DB tradeoffs (to present):
   - Pinecone (managed): best for short time-to-live and read-heavy QPS; easier ops but can't host PII docs if Lumina disallows external hosting.
   - Milvus (self-hosted on GKE): full control over data residency; higher ops cost and potentially higher tail latency during heavy egress/backfill.
   - Hybrid: hot in Pinecone, PII and cold in Milvus with cross-store routing — adds complexity but matches Lumina's constraints.

3) Rerank evaluation plan (proposal):
   - Sample: 5k queries as provided; hold out 15% as validation; use 1k queries for human annotation (stratified by intent and frequency).
   - Metrics: nDCG@10 and MAP@10 primary; MR@1 secondary. Pass threshold: >= 15% relative MAP improvement over baseline OR absolute MAP@10 >= 0.32 (whichever is easier to operationalize).
   - Smoke criteria: p95 query latency w/ reranker < 250ms in staging; end-to-end 95th < 400ms in production after gating.

4) Rollback & fallback:
   - Immediate fallback: route queries to BM25 + legacy ranker for any traffic region failing quality SLOs.
   - Backout: use snapshot of prior index and restore routing within 30 minutes given autoscaling of dedicated pools.

Ops & capacity notes (Ben): please confirm Dedicated pool sizing for initial waves — estimate: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs for parallelized embed generation and rerank scoring during backfill, then scale down to 1 reserved instance for steady-state.

Deliverables before Wed kickoff: updated MOP with wave schedule and a short runbook for the rollback steps. I'll attach a one-page decision brief to the Drive link Camila shared.

Marissa
Implementation Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
